title: Who Decides When the Network Decides?
concept: As autonomous networks progress toward L4 and L5, accountability for AI-driven decisions must remain with humans, not the model. Guardrails define approval thresholds by criticality, scope and reversibility. NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, TM Forum and ETSI ZSM all emphasize human oversight, risk-based decision rights and auditable evidence that a person owns the consequences.
why: Your unified framework must define who owns autonomous decisions, what requires human approval and how evidence proves accountability. TM Forum, NIST and ISO all treat this as a control, not a prompt.
question: Which network changes will your framework allow autonomously, which need approval, and who signs the policy defining the threshold?
